blocks.text: You can connect your Salesforce organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance to gain continuous visibility and governance for third-party apps installed in the Salesforce environment, including automation of your vetting and governance processes.
A user with Admin privileges in the relevant Salesforce organization is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to your Salesforce organization.
To connect your Salesforce organization to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: Click Connect in the upper-right corner of the App Dashboard.
From the drop-down menu, select Salesforce.
In the Add Integration window, click Add. You are prompted to sign in if you haven't already done so.
Click Sandbox to log in to your Salesforce Sandbox account.
A consent window appears (all privileges are read-only), and you can see a detailed list of permissions and data.

blocks.text: You must select the SSPM Scan checkbox on the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console to enable the SSPM scan feature for the tenant. To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant. During this time, a message displays indicating that the integration is still being processed. After integration is completed, a success message appears, and the tenant details are updated on the Settings page. You then receive an email from Zscaler when the integration is ready for further review.
You can view the list of added tenants along with information such as integration status, enabled features, first connected time, last synced time, etc. on the Settings page.
You might need to reconnect Salesforce to 3rd-Party App Governance if an error displays (e.g., Grant Expired). To reconnect Salesforce to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Reconnect icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A consent window appears. After consent is granted, the connection is updated.
You can edit a Salesforce connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To edit a Salesforce connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Edit icon next to the relevant integration.
In the Edit Integration window, edit the tenant details as required and click Save.

blocks.text: You can delete a Salesforce connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To delete a Salesforce connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Delete icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: The following table lists the permissions and data collected after integration:

table: Manage user data via APIs. It allows access to the currently logged-in user’s account using APIs, such as REST API and Bulk API 2.0. This scope also includes chatter_api, which allows access to Connect REST API resources.
Manage user data via web browsers. It allows use of access_token on the web. This scope also includes Visualforce, allowing access to customer-created Visualforce pages.
